newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU sugar committee to study set-aside yeast plan.
newsitem.headline: EU sugar committee to study set-aside yeast plan.

text.p: A plan to allow non-sugar crops intended for yeast production to be grown on set-aside land is due to be studied by the European Union's sugar management committee on Wednesday, an EU member state official said.
"The committee will discuss the possible impact on the sugar industry," the official said on Monday.
The EU's cereals management committee is due in May to discuss a draft proposal to allow farmers to use set-aside land to grow crops for yeast production.
Under the 1992 reform of the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) a programme of setting aside land to limit cereals cultivation was introduced to cut excess production.
